UPSTREAM: arch/x86: drop special case cbfs locator CBFS used to have a special region for the x86 bootblock, which also contained a pointer to a CBFS master header, which describes the layout of the CBFS. Since we adopted other architectures, we got rid of the bootblock region as a separate entity and add the x86 bootblock as a CBFS file now. The master header still exists for compatibility with old cbfstool versions, but it's neatly wrapped in either the bootblock file or in a file carefully crafted at the right location (on all other architectures). All the layout information we need is now available from FMAP, a core part of a contemporary coreboot image, even on x86, so we can just use the generic master header locator in src/lib/cbfs.c and get rid of the special version. Among the advantages: the x86 header locator reduced the size of the CBFS by 64 bytes assuming that there's the bootblock region of at least that size - this breaks assumptions elsewhere (eg. when walking CBFS in cbfs_boot_locate() because the last file, the bootblock, will exceed the CBFS region as seen by coreboot (since it's CBFS - 64bytes).
